title: Codex workers: grant linked-worktree git metadata via --add-dir, keep the sandbox
description:
Production finding (tick s8u): codex workspace-write cannot commit in a linked worktree — git metadata lives under the main repo .git/worktrees/, outside the sandbox — so the worker could not complete its durable contract (orchestrator committed on its behalf). The queued danger-full-access fix is WRONG per herdr-kinds.md own argument (it removes the sandbox entirely; only appropriate inside an already-sandboxed environment). The right mechanism is the one the doc already names: --add-dir for legitimate out-of-worktree writes.

Implement: at spawn time, for a codex-kind worker, append `--add-dir <git-common-dir>` to the compiled argv, where git-common-dir is resolved from the actual repo (git rev-parse --git-common-dir from the repo root — do not hardcode .git; respect non-default layouts). Design the mechanism cleanly rather than an if-kind==codex special case in spawn: prefer extending internal/herd/config so a kind row can declare computed per-spawn extras given a context struct (e.g. {GitCommonDir string}), compiled into Spawn.Argv like everything else — read kinds.go/compile.go/spawn.go and pick the seam that keeps "Spawn.Argv is passed verbatim" true; explain your choice. Argv order doc (runners-config.md "Args order matters") must be updated to name the computed extras position. Update herdr-kinds.md: the codex row + full-auto section gains the linked-worktree caveat (dated observation, 2026-08-12) and the --add-dir git-common-dir mechanism; fix the runners-config.md:291 compiled-argv example line accordingly. Update the byte-for-byte doc round-trip tests in internal/herd/config (docexamples_test) to the new expectation. Tests: compile for codex with a context produces the --add-dir element with the resolved path; claude kind unaffected; missing context (e.g. no repo) fails closed with a clear error rather than emitting a sandbox that cannot commit.

Boundaries: internal/herd/config, internal/herd/spawn, the two reference docs, their tests. Full-suite gate on real exits; gofmt/vet clean; do NOT commit your RESULT file.
acceptance_criteria: A codex spawn argv carries --add-dir <resolved git common dir>; sandbox flags unchanged otherwise; claude spawns unaffected; docs + byte-asserted examples updated together; fail-closed on unresolvable git dir; full suite green
